1.note: The setting changes here to focus on what is happening in Canaan. Some languages use a special conjunction (like **Now**) to indicate that, while others do not use a conjunction here. Alternate translation: [The food shortage]

The word **heavy** is used here as an idiom that means the famine caused everyone much suffering. See how you translated the same idiom in Genesis 12:10 and Genesis 41:31. Alternate translation: [was oppressive]
Alternate translation: [in the land of Canaan]

2.note: The author is using the word translated **And it happened** to introduce a new development in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new development.
Consider whether it is clearer in your language to use a pronoun or a noun phrase here. Alternate translation: [when Jacob and his family had finished eating] or [… had used up]
The pronoun **they** refers here to Jacob’s sons, not Jacob’s family (as it did earlier in this sentence). Alternate translation: [all the grain that his sons had bought and brought home]
Alternate translation: [their father Jacob told them] or [he told them]
Alternate translation: [and buy some more food]
The pronoun **us** includes Jacob and his sons and their families here. Alternate translation: [for our family]

3.note: The brothers did not realize yet that Joseph was the governor they had spoken to in Egypt, so Judah referred to him generally here as “the man.” See how you translated a similar phrase in Genesis 42:30. Alternate translation: [The man who governs the country there]
Alternate translation: [sternly told us] or [was serious when he warned us]

Consider whether it is better in your language to translate this embedded quote as a direct or indirect quote. Alternate translation: [that we cannot see him again] or [that we cannot come to him again to buy grain]

Make sure that the way you translate this clause fits with how you translated the previous part of this sentence. For some languages it is necessary to put this clause before the previous clause and say, “… that our youngest brother must be with us or else we will not be permitted to see him again!” Alternate translation: [unless our youngest brother is with us!]

4.note: In verses 3–5, the pronouns **us** and **we** are exclusive since they do not include Jacob (whom Judah is talking to). Alternate translation: [So if you will permit our youngest brother to go with us] or [So if you will let our youngest brother go with us]
Alternate translation: [then we can travel to Egypt]
Alternate translation: [and buy more grain for you and the rest of the family]

5.note: See how you translated **send** in verse 4. Alternate translation: [allow him to go with us]
See how you translated **go down** and “went down” in Genesis 42:2–3. Alternate translation: [we cannot go down there] or [we must not go there to buy grain]
Alternate translation: [because the man told us]
See how you translated this quote in verse 3. Alternate translation: [that we cannot see him again] or [that we cannot go to him again to buy grain]
See how you translated this clause in verse 3. Alternate translation: [unless our youngest brother is with us!]

6.note: If it is not clear that **Israel** (verse 6) and “their father” (verse 2) refer to the same person, you could include “their father” here in your translation or in a footnote. See what you did for a similar case in Genesis 42:5.

Jacob uses a rhetorical question here to scold his sons and to show how upset he is. Consider what is the best way to communicate that in your language. Alternate translation: [Why did you cause distress for me by telling] or [You caused me a lot of distress because you told]
See how you translated **the man** in verses 3 and 5. Alternate translation: [that man] or [that governor]
If you translate this rhetorical question as a statement, make sure that you end it with a period or exclamation point. Alternate translation: [that you have another brother!]

7.note: Alternate translation: [The man questioned us intensely] or [The man asked us many questions]

In verses 7–8, the pronouns “us,” “our,” and **we** are exclusive since they do not include Jacob (whom the sons are talking to). Alternate translation: [about ourselves and about the rest of our family]

7.q: הַ⁠ע֨וֹד אֲבִי⁠כֶ֥ם חַי֙ הֲ⁠יֵ֣שׁ לָ⁠כֶ֣ם אָ֔ח
7.note: Consider whether it is more natural in your language to translate this embedded quote with a direct or indirect quote. Alternate translation: [He specifically asked us whether our father was still alive and if we had another brother]
Alternate translation: [So we just answered his questions honestly] or [All we did was answer his questions]

Jacob’s sons use a rhetorical question here to emphasize their innocence and express strong emotion. Consider what is the best way to communicate that in your language. Alternate translation: [We could not possibly have known]

If you translate this rhetorical question as a statement, make sure that you end it with a period or exclamation point. Alternate translation: [that he would tell us to bring our brother down there to him!]

8.note: For some languages it is necessary to make “Benjamin” explicit here in the quote margin so that it is clear that **young man** refers to him in the following quote.

See how you translated **young man** in Genesis 37:2; 41:12. Use a term here in your language that fits with the fact that Benjamin was probably in his 30’s. Alternate translation: [Allow the young man to come with me and I will watch over him]
Alternate translation: [so we can leave right away to buy grain in Egypt]
See how you translated **will live and not die** in Genesis 42:2. Alternate translation: [Then all of us, including our children, will survive] or [… can stay alive]
Alternate translation: [and not die from hunger]

9.note: Alternate translation: [I personally guarantee to keep him safe] or [I personally guarantee his safety]
See how you translated a similar idiom in Genesis 31:39. Alternate translation: [You can make me liable for him]
Consider what is the best way to translate this hypothetical sentence in your language. Alternate translation: [so that if I do not bring him back home to you alive]
Alternate translation: [you can blame me for this sin]
Alternate translation: [all the days of my life] or [forever]

10.note: This sentence refers to something that could have happened, but did not actually happen. Consider what is the best way to translate this contrary-to-fact statement in your language. Alternate translation: [As it is, if we had not delayed such a long time] or [In any case, if we had not delayed this long]
Alternate translation: [certainly we could have made two round trips there and back by now] or [we certainly would have had enough time to go down there and back two times already]

11.note: See how you translated **Israel their father** in verse 8.
Alternate translation: [If that is how it must be] or [Okay, if that is the only way we can get more grain]
Alternate translation: [then this is what you must do:]
Alternate translation: [Put some of the best goods from our land in your sacks] or [Put in your sacks some of the most valuable things that our land produces]
Alternate translation: [and take them to the man in Egypt]
Consider what punctuation is best to use here in your language.

Consider what is the best way to make a list of things like this in your language. Also see how you translated **balm** in Genesis 37:25. Alternate translation: [including some sweet-smelling tree sap, some honey] or [Include some healing salve, honey]

The **pistachio nuts and almonds** are kinds of foods, in fact, delicacies. If your readers would not be familiar with what they are, you could use the names of similar things that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and some sweet-tasting tree nuts] or [and other delicacies]
See how you translated **spices** and **myrrh** in Gen 37:25. Alternate translation: [some food spices and incense]

12.note: Alternate translation: [Also take with you twice as much silver as you took the first time]
Alternate translation: [because you must give back the silver] or [You must give back the silver]
Consider whether it is better in your language to use a passive or active clause here. Alternate translation: [that was given back to you by someone]
See how you translated a similar phrase in Genesis 42:27. Alternate translation: [in the top of your sacks]
Alternate translation: [That might have happened by mistake] or [Maybe someone did that by mistake]

13.note: Alternate translation: [So then take your youngest brother]
See how you translated “get up and …” in verse 8. Alternate translation: [and return right away to the man] or [and immediately go back to the man]

14.note: The Hebrew text is ambiguous here. It could mean: (1) “so that he will” or “and I pray that the man/governor will” or (2) “and may he/God” or “and I pray that God will”

Notice that **other brother** refers to Simeon, who is older or younger (and has the same or different mother) than his brothers that Israel is talking to here. Also see how you translated **send** in verses 4–5. Alternate translation: [allow your other brother and Benjamin to go] or [let your brothers Simeon and Benjamin go]
The pronoun **I** is emphatic here in the Hebrew text. If possible, keep that emphasis in your translation. Alternate translation: [As for me, if I]
See how you translated **bereaved** in Genesis 42:36. Alternate translation: [must be deprived of them, then I will be deprived] or [must suffer loss, then I will suffer loss]

14.q: וְ⁠אֵ֣ל שַׁדַּ֗י יִתֵּ֨ן לָ⁠כֶ֤ם רַחֲמִים֙ לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י הָ⁠אִ֔ישׁ
14.note: Alternate translation: [be kind to you as you go before the man] or [cause the man to be kind to you] or [cause him to treat you mercifully]

15.note: See how you translated **gift** in verse 11 and in Genesis 33:10–11. Alternate translation: [So the brothers packed those gifts in their sacks] or [So the brothers got all those gifts and packed them]

See how you translated this phrase in verse 12. Alternate translation: [along with twice as much silver as the grain would cost] or [and they also packed double the amount of silver that they needed to pay for the grain]

See how you translated “get up and go” in verse 8. Alternate translation: [They also got Benjamin and together they immediately traveled down to the country of Egypt] or [Then they took Benjamin with them and immediately traveled down to the country of Egypt]
Alternate translation: [and presented themselves to Joseph] or [and came directly to Joseph]

16.note: Alternate translation: [Joseph saw Benjamin with the rest of his brothers. So he told] or [When Joseph saw Benjamin with his other brothers, he told]
Alternate translation: [the servant who managed his household]
Alternate translation: [Lead the men to my house]

The Hebrew word for **animal** here is general and refers to an animal that was raised to be killed and eaten, such as a calf or goat. Alternate translation: [then kill one of my livestock] or [Then butcher an calf]
Alternate translation: [and cook the meat to prepare a meal] or [and prepare a feast with its meat]
Alternate translation: [because I have planned that the men will eat the noon meal with me at my house]

17.note: Alternate translation: [The servant did exactly what Joseph had commanded him to do]
Make sure that the way you translate this phrase does not sound like Joseph’s brothers went inside the house yet. They did not actually go inside until later (verse 24).

18.note: Alternate translation: [Then they said to each other]

18.q: עַל־דְּבַ֤ר הַ⁠כֶּ֨סֶף֙ הַ⁠שָּׁ֤ב בְּ⁠אַמְתְּחֹתֵ֨י⁠נוּ֙ בַּ⁠תְּחִלָּ֔ה אֲנַ֖חְנוּ מֽוּבָאִ֑ים
18.note: Alternate translation: [We have been brought here because of the money that was returned to us in our sacks the first time we came here] or [He has taken us here because of our silver that someone gave back to us in our sacks on our first trip here]
Consider what is the best way to translate these idioms in your language. Alternate translation: [He is planning to seize us by force]
Alternate translation: [and keep us as slaves] or [and make us his slaves]
Alternate translation: [He will also take our donkeys!]

19.note: Alternate translation: [So they went up to] or [So they approached]
See how you translated a similar phrase in verse 16.
Alternate translation: [to speak to him at the door to his house] or [outside the door to the house in order to speak to him]

20.note: Alternate translation: [They said to him] or [One of them said to him on behalf of them all]

The brothers are asking the servant for permission to speak. Translate this in a way that is respectful in your language. Alternate translation: [Excuse me sir] or [Sir, please allow us to speak to you]
Alternate translation: [the previous time we came down here to Egypt, we came to buy some food] or [one time before this, we traveled all the way down here to Egypt and bought some food]

21.note: Judah is using the word translated as **But it happened** to introduce a new development in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new development.
See how you translated **the lodging place** in Genesis 42:27. Alternate translation: [when we arrived at the place where we stayed for the night, we opened our sacks]

Also, see how you translated “in the mouth of … sacks” in verse 12. Alternate translation: [and we were surprised to see that our bags of money were in the top of each of our sacks!] or [There in the opening of each of our sacks was the silver we had given to you for the grain!]

The silver was weighed in shekels (Genesis 20:16; 23:15–16; 37:28) to determine how much to pay for something. See how you translated **silver** in Genesis 42:25, 27, 35. Alternate translation: [The full weight of money was there!] or [The silver was all there!]
Alternate translation: [But we brought it all back] or [So we brought all that money back]
Alternate translation: [with us to return to you]

22.note: Alternate translation: [We also brought enough extra money with us] or [We have also brought additional money with us]
Alternate translation: [so that we can buy some more food now]
Alternate translation: [who gave that money back to us in our sacks] or [how our silver got into our sacks like that]

23.note: The phrase **Peace {be} to you** is a blessing that wishes someone to be well and at peace. Consider whether your language has a similar blessing or an idiom that would work well here. Alternate translation: [Be at peace,] or [All is well for you, so]
Make sure that your translation of these phrases refers to the same God, not two different Gods. Alternate translation: [The God whom you and your father worship]
Alternate translation: [must have put the silver in your sacks]
Alternate translation: [because I definitely received the silver that you paid for the grain] or [because I know that you paid me money to pay for the grain]

24.note: Consider again how you translated “wash … feet” in the book of Genesis. See 18:4; 19:2; 24:32; 43:24. Alternate translation: [and they washed the dirt off their feet]
Also, see how you translated **fodder** in Genesis 42:27. Alternate translation: [and he provided feed for their donkeys]

25.note: Alternate translation: [to give to Joseph when he got home at noon]
Alternate translation: [because they had been told] or [because someone had told them]

For some languages it is more natural to put the last half of this verse at the beginning of the verse and say, “When Joseph’s brothers heard that they were going to eat the noon meal with Joseph at his house, they got their gifts ready to give him when he came/got home.” Alternate translation: [that they were going to eat a meal with him there at his house]

26.note: Alternate translation: [When Joseph came to his house] or [When Joseph got home]
Alternate translation: [his brothers presented to him the gift that they had brought with them into the house]

See how you translated “bowed down … ground” in Genesis 42:6. Alternate translation: [Then they bowed themselves down before him with their faces to the ground to show him honor] or [Then they prostrated themselves on the ground to respect him]

27.note: Alternate translation: [Is your aged father doing well] or [Is your aged father in good health]
Alternate translation: [whom you spoke about to me before?]

28.note: The brothers refer to their father as **your servant** here to show respect to Joseph and to acknowledge his high position. Translate this phrase in a polite way that shows respect toward Joseph. Also, the pronoun **our** is exclusive here because Joseph’s brothers did not yet know that they were talking to Joseph. Alternate translation: [Yes sir, our father, who highly respects you, is still alive and blessed]

In this verse, the terms **bowed** and **bowed down** translate two different Hebrew words that together describe and emphasize the process of bowing down to the ground. Alternate translation: [Then they knelt]
See how you translated **bowed down** in verse 26. Alternate translation: [and prostrated themselves in front of him again]

29.note: Benjamin was younger than Joseph. Also, consider again how you translated the idiom “lifted … eyes” in the book of Genesis. See 13:10, 14; 18:2; 22:4, 13; 24:63–64; 31:10; [33:1](ta:33), 5; 37:25; 39:7; 43:29. Alternate translation: [Then Joseph looked up and saw his brother Benjamin] or [When Joseph looked around at them all, he saw his brother Benjamin]
Alternate translation: [who was the only other son of his own mother]

This question could be an actual question or a rhetorical question. The fact that Joseph does not wait for an answer suggests that this is a rhetorical question, especially since he already realized that the new brother in the group was Benjamin (verse 16). Alternate translation: [So this young man must be your youngest brother] or [I suppose this young man is your youngest brother]
Make sure that your punctuation here fits with the way you translated this sentence, either as a question or a statement.

See how you translated “God has been gracious to …” in Genesis 33:11. Also see how you translated **grace** in 24:12, 14, 27, 49; 39:21. Alternate translation: [I pray that God will be gracious to you]

The phrase **my son** is a kind way to address a man who is younger or of lower status; it does not mean that Benjamin was Joseph’s actual son. Also, for some languages it is necessary to put this address first in this quote. Do what is natural in your language.

30.note: Alternate translation: [Then Joseph quickly left the room] or [Then Joseph rushed out of the room]
Alternate translation: [because he was feeling deeply emotional about his brother] or [because he felt overwhelmed with emotions for his brother]

The Hebrew text is ambiguous here. It could mean: (1) “and desired/wanted to cry,” or “and felt like crying,” or “and was about to cry,” or (2) “and was looking for a place to cry,” or “and went to find a place to cry,”
Alternate translation: [so he went to his private room]
Alternate translation: [so that he could cry there]

31.note: Alternate translation: [After a while, he stopped crying, washed the tears off his face and came out of his room]
Alternate translation: [and told his servants] or [Then he told his servants]
The word **bread** refers to all the food they ate at this meal, not just bread. Alternate translation: [Serve the meal to us] or [It is time to serve the meal to us]

32.note: Alternate translation: [and the Egyptians who were eating as his guests at their own table] or [They also served food to some Egyptian guests at a separate table]

33.note: Alternate translation: [according to their age order, from oldest to youngest] or [in the order of their ages, from the firstborn to the youngest]
Alternate translation: [so they looked at each other in amazement] or [When they saw that, they were amazed and stared at one another]

34.note: As a person of high position and status, Joseph probably had his servants serve the food rather doing it himself. Decide whether you want to make that information explicit in your translation or include it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Then Joseph served his brothers food from his table]
Alternate translation: [but the amount of food that was served to Benjamin was five times more]
Alternate translation: [than the amount of food that was served to any of the rest of them]

The Hebrew verb for **became drunk** is the same word that is used in Genesis 9:21 to describe Noah when he had drunk so much wine that he had fallen asleep. Here, it probably means that they had drunk enough wine that they were feeling happy and sociable. Alternate translation: [Then they ate food, drank wine and feasted with him] or [Then they feasted and drank wine freely with him until they were very merry]
